angle: Self-regulation helps only when buyers hard-wire governance into contracts and KPIs.
linkedinPost:
Relying on vendor virtue is not a strategy.

Knowledge at Wharton outlines why AI self-regulation falls short and what governments might do. In the enterprise world, the faster lever is on the buyer side: procurement and performance management.

From deployments, here’s what actually changes behavior:
- Governance clauses with teeth: audit rights, incident reporting SLAs, and sunset triggers for repeated violations.
- Outcome-based KPIs that price risk: model accuracy plus measurable bias, complaint rates, and false positive costs.
- Kill-switch design: operational controls your team can invoke without vendor approval.

My take: Treat governance like uptime. If a vendor won’t commit to observable controls and penalties, you’re buying promises, not capabilities. And mirror it internally—assign a single owner for AI risk with authority to stop shipments.

Regulation will (and should) evolve. But you can buy accountability today—if you insist on it in the contract and the dashboard.

What’s one governance control you’d require if you had to live with the downside on your P&L? #AIStrategy #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI
